content.key_idea: Standard Jupyter reserves GPU-equipped kernels for the entire lifetime of a persistent client-server notebook session, even though the client mostly sits idle between cell executions.
content.reading_order: Left to right: Client icon and label, bidirectional HTTP/WebSocket arrow to the Jupyter Server (drawn as a server stack), then arrows out to the Notebook File and to the Jupyter Kernel with its reserved GPU(s).

summary: This figure illustrates the standard client-server architecture of Jupyter Notebook that motivates NotebookOS. A Client Jupyter Notebook (desktop icon) communicates with a Jupyter Server over a persistent user session using HTTP and WebSockets. The Jupyter Server manages the associated Notebook File and forwards code for execution to a Jupyter Kernel over ZeroMQ (0MQ); the kernel is drawn holding reserved GPU(s), highlighted in orange. The figure is a wide, sparse, icon-based diagram (client computer, server stack, document, GPU chip) with bold labeled arrows, used purely as background to set up the paper's observation that GPUs are reserved for the kernel's entire session lifetime even though usage is intermittent.
summary_zh: 该图展示传统 Jupyter Notebook 的客户端-服务器架构：客户端通过 HTTP/WebSocket 与 Jupyter Server 保持持久会话，Server 管理笔记本文件并通过 ZeroMQ 与占用 GPU 的 Jupyter Kernel 通信，用于说明 GPU 在整个会话期间被长期预留的背景问题。
